textBoxes.text: Fractals are by far my favorite topic to explore in p5.js. Here, I have explored four different techniques to generate fractals.

Computational randomness formed the basis of my first encounter with generative art.

My creative coding explorations have consistently centered on systems that incorporate elements of randomness, rather than fully deterministic compositions.

I was introduced to the work of artist *Desmond Paul Henry*[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmond_Paul_Henry] in the first p5.js class I took in 2018.

He used WW2 bomb sight computers to create mechanical randomness. His contraptions physcally plotted complex patterns.

In this section I implemented the basic walker class.

Randomly picks a direction moves in that direction per frame

Extended the walker class to support color.
 
Experimented with rendering multiple walkers.

The blur filter is my favourite. 

Whenever I feel uninspired I just experiment with the blur filter.

I wanted to explore multiples axis of randomness in this composition.
 
I started by randomly plotting points on the canvas.

I implemented non uniform randomness to spawn points more towards the centre. 

I wanted to explore how the walker could interact with the points. Everytime a walker hits a point it should activate.
I am taking a class with the *Ken Perlin*[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Perlin] himself. I had to implement Perlin noise in some way!
I experimented with different kinds of walkers and different visual variations of the points activation
